text: Hear now what the LORD says: Rise, plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.
Hear, you mountains, the LORD's accusation, and you enduring foundations of the earth; for the LORD has a case against his people, and with Israel he will contend.
My people, what have I done to you? How have I wearied you? Answer me!
I brought you up out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery, and I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
My people, remember what Balak king of Moab devised, and how Balaam son of Beor answered him, and what happened from Shittim to Gilgal, that you may know the saving deeds of the LORD.
With what shall I come before the LORD, and bow down before God on high? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
He has told you, O man, what is good, and what the LORD requires of you: only to do justice, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God.
The voice of the LORD cries out to the city—and it is wisdom to fear your name: Heed the rod, and the One who appointed it!

versions.text: The voice of the LORD cries out to the city—and it is wisdom to fear your name: Hear, O tribe, and you assembly of the city!
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "Hear the rod (מַטֶּה) and who appointed it," continuing the judgment imagery of the chastening rod. Rendering it "Hear, O tribe, and you assembly of the city" follows a conjectural emendation of the consonantal text (מִי יְעָדָהּ read as מוֹעֵד הָעִיר) and loses the connection with the coming punishment described in vv. 13–15. The suggested wording follows the received text and reads smoothly aloud.

text: Are there still in the house of the wicked the treasures of wickedness, and the scant measure that is accursed?

versions.text: Am I still to overlook the treasures of wickedness in the house of the wicked, and the short measure that is accursed?
versions.explanation: The Hebrew is most naturally an interrogative about what is still present in the wicked house rather than about God overlooking it; "scant measure" also renders אֵיפַת רָזוֹן (the shrunken ephah) more idiomatically than "short measure." Either reading is defensible, but the suggested form stays closer to the text while remaining easy to read aloud.

text: Can I acquit anyone who uses dishonest scales, with a bag of false weights?
Her rich men are full of violence, her inhabitants speak lies, and their tongues are deceitful in their mouths.
So I in turn have begun to strike you down, to lay you waste for your sins.
You will eat but not be satisfied; hunger will gnaw within you. You will store up but save nothing, and what you do save I will give to the sword.
You will sow but not reap; you will press olives but not anoint yourself with oil; you will crush grapes but drink no wine.

For you have kept the statutes of Omri and all the practices of the house of Ahab, and you have walked in their counsels. Therefore I will give you over to ruin, and your inhabitants to derision; you will bear the scorn of my people.

versions.text: For you have kept the statutes of Omri and all the practices of the house of Ahab, and you have walked in their counsels. Therefore I will give you over to ruin, and your inhabitants to derision; you will bear the scorn of the nations.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has עַמִּי, "my people" (singular with first-person suffix), not "the nations" (which would require an emendation to עַמִּים). The received text should be followed; the point is that the covenant people themselves bear the LORD's reproach.
